newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends 4-day winning streak with modest loss.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends 4-day winning streak with modest loss.

text.p: The Dow industrials paused in their record run Thursday, snapping a four-session winning streak on mild profit-taking and caution ahead of Friday's key September employment report.

"Stocks and bonds are waiting to see the employment report and that will set the tone for stocks for the next three weeks, along with earnings reports. Today, people are just positioning themselves," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
After surging 65 points over the past four trading days, the Dow Jones industrial average slipped 1.12 points to 5,932.85. The blue-chip index set back-to-back records on Tuesday and Wednesday.
In the broader market, declining issues outpaced advances by 1,231 to 1,106 with 386 million shares traded on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 1.23 to 692.78 after scoring its third consecutive record finish on Wednesday.
The NYSE Composite index was off 0.40 at 370.14 after snaring its fifth straight record on Wednesday. The average price per share fell 4 cents.
The technology-rich Nasdaq Composite index slipped 3.02 to 1,233.09 after rallying 15 points on Wednesday.
The key 30-year Treasury bond edged up 1/32, leaving the yield unchanged at 6.84 percent -- the lowest since Aug. 22.
Both stock and bond markets barely reacted to economic data out Thursday, focusing instead on Friday's jobs report.
Economists expect September payrolls to rise 166,000, a considerably tamer rate of growth than August's 250,000 increase and the more than 200,000 each month since May.
"We are not expecting a surprise and any surprise would hit the market hard," said Harry Laubscher of Tucker Anthony.
"We are well into overbought territory. But fund managers are quite bullish and optimistic about tomorrow's report ...," said Laubscher, a market analyst.

Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co., pointed to the American Stock Exchange's securities broker dealer index, which rose 2 to 425.04 after hitting a record high of 426.10 earlier.
"That's one group that has not been able to record new bull market highs in the past four months and it's usually a good indicator of the health of the market," he said.
Among the index's components, Schwab rose 1 to 24-1/2.
A.G. Edwards slipped 3/8 to 29-3/4 after hitting a 52-week high of 30-3/4, and Merrill Lynch slipped 1/4 to 68-3/4.

Tobacco shares fell after the Florida Supreme Court ruled that a class-action suit against the industry could proceed to a trial next spring. The state's highest court rejected a tobacco industry plea to scuttle the case.

Defendants include Dow component Philip Morris, off 1-1/8 to 91-1/4; R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings, which fell 3/8 to 26-1/2; Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries, off 1/4 to 13-1/2 in U.S. trading; and Lorillard Tobacco, a unit of Loews Corp., up 1/4 to 79-1/2.
Monsanto rose 1-1/4 to 39-7/8 after PaineWebber said it expected surprisingly stronger third-quarter earnings.

Among those warning of earnings shortfalls, EIS International, a maker of phone call processing systems, tumbled 5-1/8 to 7-7/8, Peak Technologies slumped 9-7/8 to 11-7/8, and Wall Data shed 9-1/4 to 14.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.75 to 572.60.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,811.494, down 9.006, or 0.13 percent.
